question:
**Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error.'**

Eddie just panics / when it gets close / nearer the end.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the redundancy created by using both "**close**" and "**nearer**."
 
• "**Close**" and "**near**" have similar meanings, so using both is unnecessary and incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**it gets close to the end**" or "**it gets nearer the end**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Eddie just panics when it gets close to the end."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 4: "Eddie just panics"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "when it gets close"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in Option 1.
